Lagos, imagined study

The house
that breathes.

A speculative residence organised around shade, cross ventilation and rooms that never quite end at the wall.

Climate
Humid tropical

Primary material
Rendered masonry

Study
Unbuilt

The plan begins with air. Two narrow courts pull the sea breeze through the centre, while deep concrete brows keep direct sun away from the glass.

There is no sealed internal corridor. Movement happens along shaded edges where the house meets its garden. Every threshold is allowed to be both inside and outside.

Shade is not the absence of light.

It is the material that makes light legible. Here, perforated blockwork breaks the afternoon into moving fragments. The pattern is functional, but the changing room it creates is the real architecture.
